headline: SchemaGhost uses AI to revive legacy apps, avoiding costly rewrites
summary: This open-source tool helps bridge the gap between old applications and updated APIs, using AI for suggestions but keeping developers in control.
details: SchemaGhost is an open-source tool designed to help legacy applications adapt to API changes without requiring complete rewrites. It acts as a compatibility layer, translating new API responses into formats the older applications can understand, thus breathing new life into forgotten software.

The tool leverages AI, specifically Alibaba's Qwen3 model running locally via Ollama, to analyze and suggest mappings between old and new JSON structures. This AI-driven approach can identify semantic relationships that simple string matching might miss, offering a faster development process.

Crucially, SchemaGhost treats AI suggestions as untrusted input, emphasizing human oversight. Developers must review, verify, and approve mappings before code generation, ensuring accuracy and preventing potential issues arising from incorrect AI proposals.

Beyond AI, SchemaGhost also includes a heuristic matching system, providing functionality even when AI inference is unavailable. This dual approach ensures reliability and offers flexibility for developers working with or without AI integration.

The project includes the core library, a command-line interface, an ASP.NET Core API, an Angular frontend, sample data, documentation, and automated tests, making it accessible for local exploration and contribution.
caption:
Legacy apps facing API changes? SchemaGhost uses AI to create compatibility layers, saving costly rewrites.

SchemaGhost is an open-source tool designed to help legacy applications adapt to API changes without requiring complete rewrites. It acts as a compatibility layer, translating new API responses into formats the older applications can understand, thus breathing new life into forgotten software.

The tool leverages AI, specifically Alibaba's Qwen3 model running locally via Ollama, to analyze and suggest mappings between old and new JSON structures. This AI-driven approach can identify semantic relationships that simple string matching might miss, offering a faster development process.

Crucially, SchemaGhost treats AI suggestions as untrusted input, emphasizing human oversight. Developers must review, verify, and approve mappings before code generation, ensuring accuracy and preventing potential issues arising from incorrect AI proposals.

Beyond AI, SchemaGhost also includes a heuristic matching system, providing functionality even when AI inference is unavailable. This dual approach ensures reliability and offers flexibility for developers working with or without AI integration.

The project includes the core library, a command-line interface, an ASP.NET Core API, an Angular frontend, sample data, documentation, and automated tests, making it accessible for local exploration and contribution.
